findings.quote: after this first movement, they should lay down the baggage
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna (***) in 'ὅταν ἐκπορευομένοις *** μετὰ τοῦτο τὸ πρῶτον τὰς μὲν ἀποσκευὰς ἀποτιθέναι'; the English reads on as if the clause were whole and supplies a smooth sense for the damaged words.
findings.proposed_fix: [gap in the Greek text here] ... first of all, they should lay down the baggage

units.note: Lacuna is in the tribunes' instructions; the rest of the chapter matches the Greek.
Opening 'No, not one of you' continues οὐδένα from ch. 28's final clause; fine.

findings.quote: were brought in naked and in chains
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna after 'δεδεμένοι γυμνοὶ ***' before 'οἱ τῆς στάσεως αἰτίαι γεγονότες εἰσήγοντο'; the English presents the sentence as complete.
findings.proposed_fix: were brought in bound and naked [gap in the Greek text here]

units.note: Content of the missing words unknown; do not supply text.
'Carthage' renders ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ Καρχηδόνι (New Carthage in context); literal, left as is.

findings.quote: he drew up a counterforce against the enemy stationed on the foothills
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna: 'ἀντέταττε *** πρὸς δὲ τοὺς εἰς τὸν αὐλῶνα καταβεβηκότας'. The object of ἀντέταττε (what he set against the foothill troops) is missing; 'a counterforce' is invented to smooth the gap.
findings.proposed_fix: he drew up [gap in the Greek text here: the troops he set] against the enemy stationed on the foothills
